display.title: Tanya Shiur 57: Chapter 23, A Chariot for Hashem and the Unity of Torah (Purim)
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Tanya shiur completing chapter 23: a mitzvah makes a Jew a chariot for Hashem's will, Torah study makes him one with Hashem, with a pre-Purim talk on unity.
display.summary_long: Shiur 57 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series, finishing Tanya chapter 23. When a Jew does a mitzvah, the limb that does it, like the hand that gives tzedakah, becomes a 'merkavah', a chariot carried entirely by Hashem's will; this is why mitzvos must be done with joy, and the Arizal said he reached his high levels through joy in mitzvos. The Avos were a chariot every moment of their lives, illustrated by the Rebbe Rashab's careful customs from childhood and the story of Rabbi Hillel of Paritch, who rose for an elderly man even in his sleep. A talk on Ahavas Yisroel and Purim follows: Haman's decree could only come when the Jews were scattered and divided, and Esther's call to gather all the Jews brought salvation. The class then returns to the text: Torah study unites a person's mind with Hashem's own wisdom and will, a unity beyond that of a chariot or of body and soul, and the light revealed through Torah study is greater than in the highest worlds. Thinking about this is the gateway to great fear of Heaven, an obligation for women as well as men, and even one who does not feel it must keep doing mitzvos.
display.lesson: Every mitzvah makes a Jew a chariot for Hashem's will, so do it with joy; and when you learn Torah, you are truly united with Hashem's wisdom, which should bring you to awe of Him.

date.note: Says 'this is 5737' on air, wishes a happy Purim, and cites the Rebbe's letter 'this week'; likely about 11 Adar (1 March 1977).

study_text.note: Second half of chapter 23 (daf 28b) to the end of the chapter; chapter 24 announced for next week.

segments.title: Tanya chapter 23: a mitzvah makes a Jew a chariot
segments.summary: The limb that does a mitzvah becomes a chariot for Hashem's will, which is why mitzvos are done with joy.

segments.title: The Arizal and the joy of mitzvos
segments.summary: The Arizal said he reached his levels in holiness through joy in doing mitzvos.

segments.title: The Rebbe Rashab's careful customs
segments.summary: Trained from childhood, his body did what Hashem wants out of habit.

segments.title: Rabbi Hillel of Paritch rises in his sleep
segments.summary: Young men tested the tzaddik, and he stood up for an elderly man while still asleep.

segments.title: Ahavas Yisroel and Purim: unity defeats the decree
segments.summary: Haman's decree could come only when the Jews were divided, and Esther's call to gather them brought salvation.

segments.title: Tanya chapter 23: Torah study and true unity with Hashem
segments.summary: Torah is Hashem's own wisdom and will, so learning it unites a person with Him and opens the gate to great fear of Heaven.

segments.title: The Rebbe Rashab's last words: 'I leave you my writings'
segments.summary: Retold by the Rebbe at a farbrengen: learning a Rebbe's teachings is the deepest bond with him.

relations.note: Opens 'on the second side of daf 28' and refers back to shiur 56; continues the Ahavas Yisroel talk begun there.
